September 24, 2026
Skip to main content
Release Highlights
September 24, 2026

Your meeting notes no longer have to stay inside Meetily. Ask your AI assistant about any meeting, and let your own scripts send notes where your team works - off by default and part of Pro. Plus summaries that stick to the facts, meeting links on Windows, and safer imports of long recordings.
Ask your AI assistant - Claude, Cursor, Windsurf and others - about any meeting: search your meetings, read transcripts and summaries, and start or stop a recording
Meetily can tell your tools the moment a summary is ready, and your own scripts can export any meeting as Markdown, so notes reach Notion, your CRM or your Obsidian vault without copy-paste
Summaries stick to the facts: no more made-up meeting dates, or people listed as attendees just because they were mentioned
meetilypro:// meeting links now work on Windows
Long imported recordings transcribe at the right speed, large imports no longer run your computer out of memory, and pause or cancel responds in seconds
Table of Contents
What's New in Pro 1.11.0

Meetily Pro 1.11.0, released on September 24, 2026, connects your meeting notes to the tools you already use. Your AI assistant (Claude, Cursor, Windsurf or any app that supports MCP) can now search your meetings and read their transcripts and summaries, and your own scripts can export notes and react the moment a summary is ready. Meetily still records and transcribes on your own Windows or Mac computer, with no bot joining the call, and the new integrations are part of Meetily Pro and off by default.

This release also makes summaries stick to the facts, brings meetilypro:// links to Windows, and makes importing long recordings faster and safer. If you are coming from Pro 1.9.2, this update brings everything below in a single upgrade.
Connect Meetily to the Tools You Use

The new integrations are part of Pro and are off by default. Nothing is connected until you turn on Integrations in Settings > PRO. That adds an Integrations tab, where you connect assistants and manage keys. Step-by-step setup with screenshots is below, and the full guide is in the Meetily developer docs
(opens in new tab)
.
Ask your AI assistant about your meetings

Meetily Pro now includes an MCP server. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the open protocol, introduced by Anthropic in 2024, that AI assistants use to connect to other apps. Connect Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Windsurf from Settings in one click when it is installed on the same computer, or add another assistant that supports MCP by hand, such as VS Code. Then ask things like "What did we decide last week?" or "What are my action items from yesterday's call?"

Your assistant can search all your meetings and read transcripts and summaries, and, if you allow it, start or stop a recording. You choose exactly what each assistant is allowed to do, and you can disconnect it at any time.

Meetily hands your meetings to the assistant on your own computer. What happens next is up to the assistant: most send what they read to their own AI provider, as they do with anything else you ask them. Connect the ones you already trust with your meeting notes, and check how each AI provider handles your data if you are not sure.
Step-by-step guides: the Meetily MCP server, connect Claude Desktop or Claude Code, and use your meetings in Cursor, Windsurf or Codex.
Send your notes where your team works

Meetily can now tell your tools the moment a summary is ready or, with the Record permission, a recording ends, using webhooks signed with HMAC-SHA256 so your script can check they came from Meetily. The meetily-pro command-line tool, which ships inside the app, lets your own scripts export any meeting as Markdown, text or JSON and, with a key that has the Record permission, start or stop recordings, so your notes can reach Notion, your CRM or your Obsidian vault without copy-paste. Meetily does not post to those apps itself; your script does.
For example, this exports a meeting's title, summary and timestamped transcript as Markdown:
Code language:
bash
meetily-pro meetings export <meeting-id> --format md

You create a key for each script or tool, give it only the permissions it needs, turn on its Allow switch, and can revoke it at any time. Every command is on the Meetily CLI page, and Meetily workflows has recipes for Obsidian, Notion, Jira, Slack and your CRM.
Summaries That Stick to the Facts

The default summary now only includes what was actually said. It no longer lists someone as an attendee just because their name came up, or fills in a meeting date nobody mentioned. Long meetings now summarize in full with local or cloud AI, and summaries made with Ollama follow the settings you chose.
Meeting Links Now Work on Windows

meetilypro:// links let you open a meeting, start or stop a recording, or activate your license from an email, a calendar invite or another app. They now work on Windows as well as on Mac. On Mac, links work when Meetily is already open. Links are off by default: turn on meetilypro:// links under Settings > Integrations > Advanced, and on Windows restart Meetily once afterwards. License activation links always work.
Stability & Reliability
Imported recordings longer than about 5 minutes are no longer transcribed from slowed-down audio.

A large audio import can no longer use up so much memory that it slows down or freezes your computer. Very long files are now refused at the start instead: roughly anything over 3 hours of 48 kHz stereo audio, and less for higher-quality or multichannel files.
Pausing or cancelling a large import now takes effect in seconds instead of minutes.
Settings now explain when Speaker Diarization needs "Save Audio Recordings" turned on.
Upgrade
The app will prompt you to update via the in-app update dialog. Click "Update Now!" to install. All existing settings, recordings, and models are preserved.

After You Install: Set Up Integrations
Read the Meetily developer docs

Once Meetily Pro 1.11.0 is installed, the Meetily developer docs
(opens in new tab)
 walk you through everything in this release: turning on the Automation API, connecting Claude, Codex, Cursor or Windsurf, allowing the command-line tool, creating keys and subscribing to webhooks.
1. Turn on the Automation API

Open Settings > PRO and turn on Integrations. A new Integrations tab appears with the Automation API switch at the top. That switch is the one on/off for every assistant and key: turning it off closes the connections, while recording and processing on your computer keep going.

children.alt: Meetily Settings, Integrations tab: the Automation API switch turned on, above the AI Assistants (MCP) list with Connect buttons for Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Windsurf

children.text: 2. Connect your AI assistant and choose what it can do

Click Connect next to Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Windsurf and choose what it may do. New connections start read-only; recording and editing summaries are separate switches, and no assistant can delete meetings through Meetily. Then turn on the assistant's Allow switch and restart the assistant so it loads the Meetily tools. VS Code and other MCP clients can be added by hand.

children.alt: The Claude Desktop permissions panel in Meetily: Read is always on, with separate switches for Record (start and stop the microphone), Write (edit summaries) and Delete (permanently delete meetings)

children.text: In this example, Record and Write are switched on. A new connection starts with only Read.
3. Allow the command-line tool

Under Apps & scripts, turn on Allow the CLI on this computer. That gives the built-in meetily-pro tool read-only access to your meetings and recording notifications. For a script that needs to start or stop recordings, click Create key, give it only the permissions it needs, copy the key (Meetily shows it once) and turn on its Allow switch.

children.alt: The Apps and scripts section of Meetily's Integrations tab, with the Allow the CLI on this computer switch, which gives the built-in command-line tool read-only access

children.text:
For API keys, webhooks, events and more examples, continue in the Meetily developer docs
(opens in new tab)
. For ideas on what to build, see Meetily workflows.
Frequently Asked Questions
Frequently Asked Questions

children.q: Which AI assistants work with Meetily?
children.a: Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Windsurf connect from Meetily's Settings in one click when they are installed on the same computer (Claude Code and Codex need their command-line tools installed). VS Code and other assistants that support MCP (Model Context Protocol) can be added by hand. The assistant can search your meetings, read transcripts and summaries, and start or stop a recording, limited to the permissions you give it. This needs Meetily Pro 1.11.0 or later.

children.q: Is the Meetily Automation API turned on by default?
children.a: No. The Automation API, the MCP server and webhooks are off by default, and nothing is connected until you turn them on in Settings > PRO. By default the API only listens on your own computer, and each assistant or script gets only the permissions you choose.

children.q: Can Meetily send meeting notes to Notion or a CRM automatically?
children.a: Not with a built-in connector. Meetily Pro gives your own scripts what they need instead: a signed webhook when a recording ends or a summary is ready, and a command-line tool and local API that export any meeting as Markdown, text or JSON. A short script can then send the notes to Notion, a CRM or an Obsidian vault.

children.q: Are the AI assistant and script integrations in the free Community Edition?
children.a: No. They are Meetily Pro features and are included in the 14-day Pro trial. The free, MIT-licensed Community Edition records and transcribes meetings locally and exports Markdown.

children.q: How do I update to Meetily Pro 1.11.0?
children.a: Meetily shows an in-app update dialog; click Update Now! to install. Your settings, recordings and models are kept. You can also download the 1.11.0 installer for macOS (Apple Silicon) or Windows from the Meetily Pro downloads page.
